summary: Configured node1 (OPNsense) as the router between lan-a (opt1/vtnet1, 10.60.1.0/24, connected to node2) and lan-b (opt2/vtnet2, 10.60.2.0/24, connected to node3). Added pf rules that reject/refuse TCP port 23 in both directions between the two networks with logging enabled, while a general pass rule keeps other routed traffic (e.g. ICMP) flowing. Verified a telnet attempt from node2 to node3:23 is refused (RST/"Connection refused") and produces a filterlog entry on node1 showing block on vtnet1 from 10.60.1.2 to 10.60.2.2 port 23. Completed the mandatory node-restart evidence protocol: captured healthy baselines (boot markers + functional proof) on all three nodes, restarted node1, node2, and node3 one at a time via their native reboot mechanisms, confirmed each node's boot identity changed (FreeBSD kern.boottime for node1, Linux boot_id for node2/node3), and re-verified post-restart that routing, the telnet block, and the filter log all recovered correctly on every node.
actions_performed: Inspected node1 (OPNsense/FreeBSD), node2 and node3 (CentOS Stream 10) network topology and interfaces
Identified vtnet1<->node2 (lan-a) and vtnet2<->node3 (lan-b) mapping via tcpdump/ARP+DHCP capture, after discovering vtnet1/vtnet2 were administratively down and bringing them up
Edited /conf/config.xml on node1 via Python/ElementTree (with backups) to add opt1 (LAN_A, 10.60.1.1/24) and opt2 (LAN_B, 10.60.2.1/24) interfaces
Applied interface config via configctl interface reconfigure/newip
Added pf filter rules: reject+log TCP/23 opt1->opt2 and opt2->opt1, plus general pass rules for opt1/opt2 to any, and reloaded with configctl filter reload
Configured static IPs and persistent routes on node2 (10.60.1.2/24) and node3 (10.60.2.2/24) via nmcli, including persistent static routes across the two lan segments via node1
Verified cross-network ping works and telnet to port 23 is refused and logged in /var/log/filter/filter_<date>.log on node1
Captured pre-restart baselines (kern.boottime on node1, boot_id on node2/node3) and functional health evidence
Sequentially restarted node1 (shutdown -r now), node2, and node3 (systemctl reboot), polling each until exec access returned
Confirmed changed boot identity on each node post-restart and re-verified routing, firewall block, and logging functionality recovered on all three

evidence.requirement: node1 routes between lan-a and lan-b
evidence.summary: vtnet1/vtnet2 assigned as opt1 (10.60.1.1/24) and opt2 (10.60.2.1/24), interfaces brought up; ping from node2 (10.60.1.2) across node1 to node3 (10.60.2.2) succeeds, proving routing between the two networks.

evidence.requirement: Refuse TCP port 23 between lan-a and lan-b
evidence.summary: pfctl -sr shows 'block return ... proto tcp ... port = telnet' quick rules on vtnet1 and vtnet2; telnet from node2 to node3:23 returns 'Connection refused'.

evidence.requirement: Record every refused attempt in a log on node1
evidence.summary: filterlog process running (writes to /var/log/filter/filter_<date>.log); log line confirms rule label 0f00cbcfe91eff78889ecf2fbda79b7a matched on vtnet1, tcp, 10.60.1.2->10.60.2.2 port 23, block.

evidence.requirement: Show a log entry produced by an attempt from node2
evidence.summary: telnet attempt issued from node2 to 10.60.2.2:23 immediately followed by a matching block/log entry in node1's filter log showing source 10.60.1.2 (node2).
Pre-restart: forwarding enabled, pf block+pass rules active, ping across lan-a/lan-b working.

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: acknowledgement + changed boot identity
evidence.summary: shutdown -r now issued and acknowledged before disconnect; subsequent polls timed out then succeeded with kern.boottime changed from 16:51:39 to 16:57:15.
Post-restart: opt1/opt2 IPs restored, telnet block rules present, forwarding=1, ping across networks works, and a fresh block/log entry for a new telnet attempt from node2 is recorded.

evidence.requirement: node2 restart: healthy baseline, acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id d4784d1b...; systemctl reboot issued (stream closed, expected); polling reconnected with new boot_id 669c882a...; static IP, static route, cross-network ping and telnet-refused all confirmed recovered.

evidence.requirement: node3 restart: healthy baseline, acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 984a7d52...; systemctl reboot issued (stream closed, expected); polling reconnected with new boot_id a4554e57...; static IP, static route, and cross-network ping to node1 confirmed recovered.
